_about: The U visa petition (Form I-918, src/u_visa.py), per the Form I-918 Instructions (01/20/25, 'Required Initial Evidence' 1-8 and 'Supplement A and Evidence to Support Supplement A') and uscis.gov/i-918 (updated 06/05/2026): the G-28 and the I-918, the ORIGINAL signed Supplement B inserted by hand right after it, a Supplement A per qualifying family member and the I-192 when the client is inadmissible (src/u_visa.py forms_for drops the others), then the evidence in the Instructions' order: the victim, the abuse, the information, the helpfulness, the crime is qualifying, the personal statement, the waiver; then identity, the family members' relationship documents, court and USCIS papers. Mailed to the lockbox for the client's state (Attn: 1367). The attorney approves titles and order.
title: U visa petition (I-918)
requires_message: The client hasn't been processed yet: process the client first.

handwork.text: The ORIGINAL Supplement B, signed by the certifying official in the last six months, right after the I-918: never a copy (I-918 Instructions, Required Initial Evidence 1; Supplement B Instructions).
I-918 Part 3 (and Part 5 of each Supplement A): every question answered with the client. A Yes may make the client inadmissible: then Form I-192 goes with it.
Foreign-language documents: each with a full English translation and the translator's certification (I-918 Instructions, Translations).
The work permit for the bona fide determination: USCIS recommends filing Form I-765 with the I-918, no fee (uscis.gov/i-918, questions 8 and 10).

exhibits.title: Evidence the client is a victim of qualifying criminal activity: police reports, court documents, orders of protection, trial transcripts, news articles, affidavits
Evidence of the substantial physical or mental abuse suffered: medical and counseling records, photographs of injuries, reports of professionals, witness affidavits
Evidence the client has information about the criminal activity: reports and affidavits of police, judges and other officials
Evidence of the client's helpfulness to the investigation or prosecution: court documents, reimbursement forms for travel to court, affidavits
Evidence the criminal activity is qualifying and occurred in the United States or violated U.S. law: the statute's elements
For the waiver (Form I-192): the client's own police and court records and the evidence supporting the waiver
Identity and age: passport, birth certificate (with certified English translation), Form I-94
Supplement A: each family member's relationship documents (marriage, birth, divorce or death certificates)
